name: Hidden SSID does not provide security

technical_body.reason: Clients that have ever seen the network volunteer the SSID in probe requests on association attempts. The SSID leaks by design.
technical_body.posture: Hiding SSID is a configuration convenience; it must not be treated as an access control.

name: PMF-required (MFPR bit set) as a hardening posture

technical_body.role: Best-practice for any WPA3 or WPA2-Enterprise deployment where all clients support PMF
technical_body.cost: Excludes legacy PMF-incapable clients from associating

technical_body.role: Delivered in M3; instructs the client to disable WPA2 fallback for this network permanently
technical_body.limitation: Only clients that honor the KDE benefit — many do not

technical_body.role: Devices unable to speak 802.1X authenticate by MAC address only — a common IoT accommodation
technical_body.risk: MAC spoofing bypasses trivially; treat MAB VLANs as untrusted

technical_body.role: The load-bearing defense against rogue RADIUS. Client profile pins the RADIUS server certificate CN + issuing CA.
technical_body.deployment: MDM-enforced (Intune, Jamf, Workspace ONE) on managed devices; hard on BYOD

technical_body.signal: Two beacons observed with the same BSSID on different channels or with different IE fingerprints
AP emitting probe responses for SSIDs it does not otherwise beacon; particularly if the SSID set matches known probe-history from a single STA

false_positives: real clients moving between crowded venues

technical_body.signal: RADIUS Accounting-Start requests without matching authentication; EAPOL-Start rate above threshold at the authenticator

technical_body.role: MFPC=1, MFPR=0 — accept both PMF-capable and legacy clients
technical_body.risk: Legacy clients on the same AP remain deauth-vulnerable — attacker knocks off PMF-off clients, not the whole network

name: AP-side rate limit on management frames

technical_body.role: Enterprise APs cap the per-STA rate of probe / auth / assoc frames to defeat floods
technical_body.limitation: Set too aggressively, real clients drop association during roaming

technical_body.role: AP drops STA-to-STA frames on a bridged SSID
technical_body.limitation: Bypassed by Framing Frames (2023) and MacStealer (2023) against unpatched APs

technical_body.role: The only defense against PMKID capture + 4-way capture that does not require WPA3
technical_body.posture: 12+ chars of ?a?a?a?a?a?a?a?a?a?a?a?a is roughly the hashcat -w4 wall-time barrier for a single high-end GPU

technical_body.role: Regular RADIUS cert rotation forces re-provisioning of client profiles, which surfaces cert-pinning gaps
APs dedicated to monitor mode + a separate WIPS engine, sitting alongside serving APs

name: 6 GHz-only SSID as a hardening posture

technical_body.role: Client can only associate on 6 GHz where WPA3 is mandated and no transition mode is allowed
technical_body.closes: WPA2 downgrade path; still vulnerable to Dragonblood on weak SAE

technical_body.role: Disable Neighbor Report Response / BTM Request emission on APs where roaming is not required

name: OCI (Operating Channel Information) — KRACK partial fix

technical_body.role: Binds the negotiated operating channel into the 4-way handshake; MC-MitM on a different channel now breaks the handshake
technical_body.note: Present on modern supplicant + hostapd; still absent on some embedded stacks

technical_body.role: wpa_supplicant >= 2.7 patches KRACK; iOS 11 / Android 6.0.1+ / Windows October 2017 update also do
technical_body.gap: Embedded / IoT firmware without an update path remains vulnerable
